title: Reverse Linked List Subrange
statement:
Reverse one inclusive position range inside a singly linked list.

Contract
- `head` may be null. `start` and `end` are 1-based positions with `1 <= start <= end <= length`.
- Reverse exactly the nodes from position `start` through position `end` by rewiring `next` pointers, and return the possibly new head.
- Nodes outside the range must keep their original relative order and identity.
- Use constant extra space.

Examples
- `reverseBetween([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 2, 4)` returns `[1, 4, 3, 2, 5]`.
- `reverseBetween([1, 2, 3], 1, 3)` returns `[3, 2, 1]`.
- Reversing a one-position range leaves the list unchanged.
hints: Use a dummy node before the head so reversing from position 1 is not special.
Walk to the node immediately before the range, then repeatedly move the next node after the range front.
Each moved node becomes the new first node of the reversed segment. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: list values followed by start and end positions, for example: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] 2 4
